import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# 1. Filter for the most recent year to get a current snapshot of the dog population
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# 2. Clean data: drop rows with missing breed or age information
df_latest.dropna(subset=['Rasse1Text', 'AlterVHundNum'], inplace=True)

# 3. Identify the top 10 most popular breeds to focus the visualization
top_10_breeds = df_latest['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# 4. Filter the dataframe to include only these top 10 breeds
df_top_10 = df_latest[df_latest['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)].copy()

# 5. Shorten and clarify breed names for better readability on the plot
# Using a dictionary to map German/long names to cleaner English names
breed_map = {
    'Mischling klein (< 45 cm)': 'Small Mixed Breed (<45cm)',
    'Mischling mittel (45-60 cm)': 'Medium Mixed Breed (45-60cm)',
    'Labrador Retriever': 'Labrador Retriever',
    'Chihuahua': 'Chihuahua',
    'Jack Russel Terrier': 'Jack Russel Terrier',
    'Franz. Bulldogge': 'French Bulldog',
    'Yorkshire Terrier': 'Yorkshire Terrier',
    'Malteser': 'Maltese',
    'Golden Retriever': 'Golden Retriever',
    'Mops': 'Pug'
}
df_top_10['Breed_Clean'] = df_top_10['Rasse1Text'].map(breed_map).fillna(df_top_10['Rasse1Text'])

# Get the order of cleaned names based on the original popularity ranking
# This ensures the plot is ordered from most to least popular breed
ordered_breeds_clean = [breed_map.get(breed, breed) for breed in top_10_breeds]


# --- Visualization ---

# 1. Set plot style and figure size for a clean, professional look
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.edgecolor": ".8", "grid.color": ".9"})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 9))

# 2. Create the violin plot
# A violin plot is excellent for comparing the distribution of a numerical variable (age)
# across multiple categories (breeds).
sns.violinplot(
    data=df_top_10,
    x='AlterVHundNum',
    y='Breed_Clean',
    order=ordered_breeds_clean,
    palette='Spectral_r',
    inner='quartile',  # Shows the median and interquartile range inside the violin
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# 3. Add titles and labels for clarity and context
ax.set_title(
    f'Age Distribution of the 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds in Zurich ({latest_year})',
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25,
    loc='left'
)
fig.text(0.125, 0.92, 'Each "violin" shows the density of dogs at each age. Wider sections indicate more dogs at that age.',
         fontsize=12, color='gray')


ax.set_xlabel("Dog's Age (Years)", fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel("", fontsize=12, labelpad=15) # Y-axis label is self-explanatory

# 4. Customize aesthetics for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='y', length=0, labelsize=11) # Remove y-axis ticks
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=11)
ax.set_xticks(range(0, int(df_top_10['AlterVHundNum'].max()) + 2, 2)) # Set x-ticks every 2 years
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True) # Remove top and right plot borders

# 5. Add a grid for the x-axis for easier age reading
ax.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.set_axisbelow(True) # Ensure grid is drawn behind the violins

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for title

# Save the final figure as a high-quality PNG
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
